answer: A stake-backed identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, so spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits. Reputation accrues slowly, like a willow growing roots, and misbehavior burns the stake - a lantern that only stays lit while the agent behaves. An atlas of past attestations lets others verify history before trusting a newcomer, so cheap copies arrive with no record and no work.
